sentences.text: This appeal is preferred by the appellant/Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award passed by the Prl. Senior Civil Judge & CJM & MACT-II, Bidar, in MVC No.93/2010, dated 28.02.2014.

entities.text: Prl. Senior Civil Judge & CJM & MACT-II, Bidar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant/insurance company has filed I.A.No.1/2015 under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, to condone the delay of 174 days in filing this appeal.
4. This application is supported with affidavit of Naresh Nukalpati, Officer of National Insurance Company Ltd., Bidar.
He has stated in his affidavit that the reason for the delay was that the certified copy was obtained by making application on 19.03.2014 and was delivered on 01.04.2014 to the Advocate.
Thereafter the same was sent with the legal opinion by the Trial Court Advocate appearing for the company to the Division Office of the appellant/insurance company.

In the meantime, there were several transports of the officers in-charge of the legal section and there was shortage of staff in sorting out cases for being sent to the regional office of the company.
In the meantime, the regional manager of the company at Hubli also retired.

Thereafter the case was dispatched to the company's senior counsel for his legal opinion, and after being advised to prefer appeal on the above grounds, the file was returned to Gulbarga Division and handed over to the panel advocate of the appellant/insurance company.
The reason for loss of time stated above in preferring the appeal is genuine and is for bonafide.

There are large number of cases filed against the appellant/insurance company and this case missed out from being appealed against as there was shortage of staff due to transfers and retirement and the file could not be looked into on these genuine grounds.
If the delay is not condoned, the appellant/insurance company will be put to a great loss.
On all these grounds sought to allow the application.
5. Respondent side arguments taken as nil.

6. On hearing learned counsel for the appellant/insurance company the following points arise for consideration:
(i) Whether the appellant/insurance company has made out sufficient cause to condone the delay in filing this appeal as sought in I.A.No.1/2015?
( ii )
What order?

sentences.text:
7. My answer to the points are as under:
Point No.1 : In Negative Point No.2 : As per final order.
8.
A perusal of this appeal it is clear that the appellant/insurance company has filed this appeal on 02.12.2014.

On the date of filing of appeal, the appellant/insurance company has not filed application for condonation of delay along with memorandum of appeal i.e. on 31.08.2015 after lapse of 8 months, 29 days, the appellant has filed this application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act to condone the delay of 174 days.

The appellant/insurance company has not sought for condone the delay from the date of filing this appeal till filing of this application i.e. 31.08.2015 and the appellant has not explained anything in his affidavit in this regard.

The appellant/insurance company has not produced any document before this Court to show that the Company's Senior Counsel has given his legal opinion and the appellant has also not produced any materials to substantiate the arguments made in the affidavit.
Accordingly, the appellant/insurance company has failed to place sufficient cause to condone the delay in filing this appeal.

Hence, I answered point No.1 in Negative.
9.

For the aforesaid reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) I.A.No.1/2015 filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, for condonation of delay in filing the appeal is dismissed.
Consequently, appeal is also dismissed.
(ii) The amount in deposit, if any, by the appellant/insurance company is directed to be transmitted to the concerned Court, along with a copy of this order.

Sd/-
